_what_this_is: What good looks like, as opposed to how to compute it.
Every other file in this directory is a convention — how a figure is worked out.
`planning_parameters.md` decides whether cycle stock is D×R or D×R/2, whether DIOH
divides by 365 or by working days. None of them say what the answer should be.
So the run could measure a gap between what stock is and what it should be, and had
nothing to say about whether that gap was acceptable. `TargetPlanner` has existed
since the should-be engine did, and nothing could start it: no flag, no setting, no
field. The ordered set of moves it produces was unreachable from any surface a
_not_here_yet: Inventory turnover and an on-time-delivery target belong beside the one below and
are deliberately absent rather than stubbed. A key nothing reads is worse than a
missing one: it reads as configured, and the first person to set it would be
entitled to believe the run had taken it into account.
OTD in particular is not ready to be a target. The KPI review already refuses to
score one: where request-date discipline is poor it says so and declines, because a
target set against a number half of whose lines carry a date nobody meant is a
target met or missed by order entry. It is a measuring stick first, and the
attribution — how much of the gap stock could close at all — comes before any
_how_the_target_is_used: `inventory_target_value` is a balance-sheet figure in the reporting currency, and
it produces an ordered set of actions rather than a number: free and reversible
first (stop buying, push out inbound), then recurring cost, then service. What was
deliberately not recommended is part of the output.
`inventory_target_date` is what makes it honest. Excess stock converts to cash only
as fast as demand consumes it, so a SKU with 300 days of cover cannot contribute
its full excess by December — only the part that will actually be consumed. A
target with no date is accepted and planned without that limit, which reads as a
larger reduction than the calendar can deliver; the frontier says so where it
Both may be null. Null is not zero: no target is stated, no frontier is computed,
and the run reports what stock should be without an opinion about what it must be.
A target of 0 is a target.
